PullRequest.Title: Compact auxiliary windows: compactAllowsSplit keeps a split window compact
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349076

A compact auxiliary editor window leaves compact mode as soon as a second editor group is added, and while compact it sends new groups to the main window. The new auxiliary window option `compactAllowsSplit` keeps such a window compact when its editor area is split, and adds the new group to that window. For example, a compact chat window can show a document beside the chat:

```ts
editorService.openEditor(input, { auxiliary: { compact: true, compactAllowsSplit: true } }, AUX_WINDOW_GROUP);
```

Without the option, behavior is unchanged.

Used by #349048 (`workbench.action.newChatWindow` takes window options) for Team Tools' Agent Fix (microsoft/vscode-packages#453), which opens its report beside the chat.

**Validation:** core typecheck. Tested manually in Code OSS: the Agent Fix chat window opens the report beside the chat in the same window and stays compact (no status bar, compact title bar).

Scenarios.Scenario: Create an auxiliary editor window with compactAllowsSplit enabled, or create a window without the new option.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor group selection awaits EditorParts.createAuxiliaryEditorPart -> AuxiliaryEditorPart.create -> auxiliaryWindowService.open, then creates the editor part and opens the requested editor. Cold file content resolution must finish before that document is displayed. The new option adds Boolean state initialization, not another awaited operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open one browser/native auxiliary window, clone its styles, and load stylesheet links.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One window per explicit auxiliary-window creation; stylesheet work scales with existing style/link nodes for that window, not with compactAllowsSplit or editor-group count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same window creation and stylesheet cloning occurred once for each auxiliary-window request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Window creation is awaited; stylesheet readiness is represented by the existing styles-loaded barrier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query inherited always-on-top state when not supplied, register the auxiliary window, and query its maximized/fullscreen/always-on-top state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per native auxiliary window, zero or one inherited always-on-top query, and fixed per-window state queries (maximized query is platform-dependent).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls and placement on the window-creation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The inherited-state query, when needed, and registration are awaited; constructor state queries run asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the requested text model and read content through textFileService.readStream, ultimately fileService.readFile/readFileStream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Content resolution for the requested visible document; models are shared by resource. Existing warm-model async reload behavior can revalidate content using an etag. The new flag does not initiate a second resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The requested editor used the same text-model resolution and file-provider path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold model resolution blocks document display; existing-model async reload is off the display critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicitly requested auxiliary windows, stylesheet nodes per window, and distinct visible document resources; ordinarily one window and one initially visible editor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing async window creation sequence is unchanged; native state initialization queries are not joined to completion. The new option creates no tasks, queue, limiter, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or key space. Existing resource models and references are reused; pending cold model resolves are coordinated per resource. Warm file reloads remain asynchronous and etag-aware. Failed resolutions do not gain any new retry path or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the public editor option through editorGroupFinder, EditorParts, AuxiliaryEditorPart, browser/native window services, and text-file resolution. Changed initialization only stores a Boolean and passes it to editor-part option updates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual window-creation, stylesheet, file-provider, and extension-editor durations vary and were not measured; none of their invocation counts is increased by this initialization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added option does not change window-creation boundaries, content-resolution frequency, or concurrency; absent/false preserves the old branches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Split, open a document beside a chat/editor, toggle compact mode, resize, and remove groups in an opt-in compact auxiliary window.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Group selection/addition synchronously resolves getAddGroupLocation and creates one group in the selected grid. The requested editor is then opened through the existing editor pane. Resize uses the existing auxiliary onWillLayout handler. Explicit compact-mode transitions update existing options and chrome.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the requested editor and resolve its content through the existing editor-pane/model services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added group per add/split request and the corresponding requested editor open; existing SIDE_GROUP neighbor reuse is unchanged. Copies use the existing editor/model sharing path. No auxiliary window is created merely to split.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Compact windows redirected group creation to the main part; the same logical split/editor request created a group and opened its editor there. The PR changes destination and compact chrome, not the number of requested documents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold document content can delay the requested document display; the group grid and layout update synchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User-requested split/group operations and live groups in the destination window. This is not a loop creating a group for every editor or history entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Group routing and grid mutation remain synchronous, with the same one-group creation path. Existing editor opens are asynchronous. Skipping updateCompact(false) for opt-in splits avoids the automatic chrome/options transition rather than adding nested relayout work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Text-model sharing, per-resource pending resolution, and asynchronous warm reload remain unchanged. optionsDisposable retains at most one enforced-options registration per compact part; repeated compact option updates do not accumulate registrations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected getAddGroupLocation, resolveAddGroupLocation, EditorPart.addGroup, option enforcement, compact event handlers, and ownership/disposal. The changed conditional only retains the existing compact policy and chooses the local grid.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Layout cost depends on live groups and editor contents; no timings were measured. Keeping compact chrome while splitting is intentional functionality, not independently demonstrated extra work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No new boundary fan-out, repeated model loading, or unbounded retained collection is introduced. Existing per-group listeners and window-level cleanup were already used by split auxiliary windows; the diff does not remove disposal ownership.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save window state or an editor working set, then restore auxiliary windows after startup or working-set switching.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: State capture serializes existing editor grids and window state, adding compactAllowsSplit only when true. Normal memento persistence is driven by the existing save-state event. Startup restoration waits for main-part readiness, launches existing auxiliary-window creation promises, joins them, then joins part readiness/restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize persisted editor/window state with one optional Boolean property per opted-in auxiliary part.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing grid/state capture per persistable auxiliary window and one optional constant-sized field per opted-in window; no per-editor clone or added state traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same state objects and editor grids were captured and serialized without the optional Boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: State capture/stringification remains synchronous on existing save/working-set paths; the diff adds only bounded per-window metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/common/component.ts: onWillSaveState -> src/vs/workbench/common/memento.ts: ScopedMemento.save -> src/vs/base/parts/storage/common/storage.ts: Storage.set / flushPending
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist memento state through cached, delayed, batched database.updateItems calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing scope/key-level stores, with pending inserts coalesced by key and unchanged values suppressed; not one database write per auxiliary window or group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical save trigger, storage keys, equality suppression, batching, and database update path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Database updates are delayed/batched by the existing throttled flush mechanism; shutdown may wait for the existing flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reopen each saved auxiliary window and perform its existing registration/native state initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: W native registrations for W saved auxiliary windows, plus the same fixed per-window state queries. Splitting an opt-in window does not increase W.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All W saved auxiliary windows were already opened with Promise.allSettled over the same creation loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing concurrent window creation is joined before restoration proceeds; native registration remains awaited per window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore editor groups and resolve visible editor content through existing shared model services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing restored groups/visible editors determine resolve requests; distinct resource models are shared. The new Boolean does not add serialized editors or duplicate restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same saved grid and editor data were restored using the same model-loading path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold visible document models participate in editor restoration; existing warm async reload behavior is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: W persisted auxiliary windows, existing serialized groups/editors, and distinct visible resource models. The diff adds at most one Boolean field per opted-in auxiliary window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restoration already launches all saved auxiliary-window creations and joins Promise.allSettled, without a new global limiter or new burst from this diff. Storage flushes remain throttled and batched. Grid serialization remains synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing storage string equality checks and key-level pending-write coalescing remain intact. Resource-model reuse and pending resolve coordination remain unchanged. Restored options are read from the same existing window-state object; no new unbounded cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced createState/saveState, working-set capture, restoreState/restoreParts, memento storage, Storage.set/flushPending, and native window creation. The changed persistence expression adds only conditional metadata.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large existing workspaces can already have expensive serialization/restoration; their prevalence and timings are unknown. No changed multiplicity or scheduling mechanism amplifies those costs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Serialization has constant-sized incremental data per window, storage call cardinality is unchanged, and restoration concurrency/window counts are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all three changed files and all diff pages against base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions found. No concrete historical performance regression fix qualified for blame/report_regression_fix. Static review only; specialized editor implementations and measured durations were not profiled.
